descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P1 · our extension of a stated behaviour · ours: rapid repeated changes.

Approach · TC-06 Admission Status Toggle · S20 Quick repeated changes: the last choice wins everywhere (both contexts)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U4 The physician can change the badge by hand at any time (before or after Generate, and on a patient whose status already rolled) through all three states, and each change persists (list, chart, reload … (UAT TC-06; TFA-92584 AC 1)
  • U12 All of the above works in both Hospital and Nursing Home (step 7, ground rule 3.3) (UAT TC-06; UAT 3.3; TFA-92584 AC 7)

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Hospital patient and resident untouched

When In each chart header choose New Admission, Consult, Follow-up, New Admission one right after another; go to the list; re-open the chart and reload. Hospital, then Nursing Home

Then List and chart both show New Admission, and H&P / SNF admission is pre-selected

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): oracle.mjs: list contains New Admission and not Consult (anchors as in S01); chart New Admission and H&P / SNF admission [selected]. Run in both contexts: the select is the same component, but each context saves through its own path (rounding vs snf mutations), which is where a race would differ

Where it ran: dev unit U11; test method AGENT · Browser agent; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (automated)

S20 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Test method: AGENT · Browser agent — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: dev.
